title: DPDP Section 5 Statutory Notice Requirements for Pathology Labs (2026)
meta_description: How pathology laboratories must serve bilingual Section 5 consent notices before sample collection under DPDP Act 2023.
summary: Mandatory guidelines for drafting and presenting Section 5 notices across patient reception desks and digital kiosks.
content:
Section 5 Notice Mandate

Section 5(1) of the DPDP Act 2023 mandates that every data fiduciary must provide a clear notice before collecting personal data, outlining itemized purposes and data principal rights.

faqs.question: What languages must the notice be available in?
faqs.answer: English and any constitutional Eighth Schedule language relevant to the patient intake region.

title: Sending Medical Reports via WhatsApp: Legal DPDP Rules for Clinics
meta_description: Statutory requirements for sending PDF blood test and diagnostic reports over WhatsApp under DPDP Act 2023.
summary: WhatsApp report dispatch requires verified opt-in consent and password-protected PDF payloads to satisfy statutory data privacy rules.
content:
WhatsApp Delivery Safeguards

Dispatching unencrypted medical reports without documented consent constitutes unconsented digital processing under Section 6 of the DPDP Act.

faqs.question: Can clinics send reports on WhatsApp automatically?
faqs.answer: Only if the patient explicitly checked the communication consent box during registration.

title: DPDP Compliance Guide for Diagnostic Centres in Maharashtra (2026)
meta_description: Complete statutory guide for pathology labs and diagnostic centres in Maharashtra to achieve DPDP Act 2023 Section 5 and Section 33 compliance.
summary: Pathology laboratories across Mumbai, Pune, and Nagpur must implement Section 5 bilingual consent notices (Marathi and English) before processing blood and radiology diagnostics.
content:
Section 5 Multilingual Notice Requirements in Maharashtra

Intake software must present consent options in Marathi alongside English prior to taking patient samples.

faqs.question: Is Marathi consent notice mandatory for pathology labs in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The DPDP Act requires notices to be available in English and 8th Schedule languages.
